digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate + Gerrit DET review-bot criterion
propositions: Complex bug fixes (non-test file_impact + >150 non-test lines) currently flow to main with only advisory findings because the bug tier runs a LIGHT advisory rubric; they should escalate to the full blocking criteria when the ticket's persisted file_impact enumerates any non-test path.

The bug tier escalation must apply deterministically at review time (no diff exists yet) by keying on the ticket's declared file_impact, derived at a single routing seam (orchestrator.route_criteria) reachable by both the precheck step and the batch-runner's project-criteria fan-in.

Gerrit DET must backstop oversized bug fixes lacking current-or-code-drifted attestation with a blocking finding; it must verify the attestation cross-host using opcert machinery and the trusted_env keyring, never via own-env plan_review_status, and accept only certified or code-drifted verdicts.

The attestation verdict predicate must accept {certified, stale-code, stale-head}, flag {unsigned, wrong-kind, malformed-pin, malformed-phase, stale-material, stale-reopened, stale-pin-drift, stale-pin-missing, unverifiable-material, incompatible-phase, mismatch, key_not_valid_at_era, unknown_kind, unknown_scheme, invalid}, and fail open (advisory only) on {unavailable, error, unknown-future}.

Non-test line classification (tests/** or conftest.py excluded; everything else counts as non-test) and the 150-line threshold must be embodied in a single shared module-level constant used by both B1 enforcement and the B2 backtest.

A backtest against 113 historical bug-fix commits must confirm that the non-test classification + 150-line threshold flags exactly the 13 commits adjudicated substantive and none of the remaining 100 mechanical changes (rename/move/format/generated churn).
